summary.one_liner: A curated, alphabetized index of software engineering blogs from companies, individual engineers, and technology projects, with an OPML file of RSS feeds.
summary.what_it_does: The README is an awesome-style list of links rather than a software project. It is organized into three sections (Companies, Individuals/Group Contributors, and Products/Technologies), each split into alphabetical subsections by first letter. The company section lists corporate engineering blogs such as Airbnb, GitHub, Netflix, Stripe, and Spotify, and the individuals section lists personal engineering blogs such as Martin Fowler, Dan Luu, and Julia Evans. The technologies section lists blogs tied to tools like Go, Rust, Kotlin, and Swift. The README also points to an OPML file for importing all listed feeds into an RSS reader. It has no install or run steps.
use_cases: find engineering blogs from tech companies
subscribe to engineering blog RSS feeds
discover blogs about specific languages or technologies
import a list of engineering blogs into a feed reader
how_to_run: Open the README and browse the company, individual, or technology lists
Import the engineering_blogs.opml file (linked in the README) into an RSS reader
notable: Alphabetized index of company engineering blogs, individual contributors, and technology blogs
Provides an OPML file for importing all feeds into an RSS reader
Covers a wide range of companies from Airbnb and Netflix to smaller firms
Includes personal blogs by well-known developers such as Martin Fowler, Dan Luu, and Julia Evans
caveats: Link list only; it contains no software to run
Entries are listed by name only in the README, with no descriptions or dates, so the list may go stale
